physical_harm: Rape and murder resulting in death
key_evidence_accepted: The prosecution successfully established the charge of the offence of rape, punishable under Section 376 of the IPC as well as the offence under Section 366 of IPC. The appellant–accused was also convicted for the offence under Section 302.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the witnesses based on the evidence presented, which included the testimony of the maternal uncle of the deceased and the findings of the prosecution regarding the offence.

legal_representation.accused: K. Parameshwar, Shekhar G Devasa, Manish Tiwari, Ms. Thashmitha Muthanna, Prashant Dixit, Vishwanath Chaturvedi, Shashi Bhushan, Sunil Ambavelil for M/s. Devasa & Co., Advs.
legal_representation.state: Shubhranshu Padhi, Vishal Banshal, Ms. Rajeshwari Shankar, Niroop Sukrithy, Ovias Moh., Advs.

appeal_history.high_court: Dismissed the appeal preferred by the appellant challenging the conviction and sentence
appeal_history.supreme_court: Partly allowing the appeal, the Court modified the order of sentence of the Trial Court for the offence punishable under Section 302 of the IPC and directed that the appellant shall undergo imprisonment for life and be released only after completing thirty years of actual sentence

prosecution_argument: The State Government preferred an appeal for enhancement of the sentence, arguing that the Constitutional Courts are not powerless to impose modified sentences considering the gravity of the offence, the conduct of the accused and other relevant factors even though the death penalty has not been imposed.
defence_argument: The appellant contended that in view of the law laid down by the Constitutional Bench in the case of Union of India v. V. Sriharan alias Murugan & Ors., a modified sentence can be imposed only by the Constitutional Courts and not by the Sessions Courts. He also relied upon decisions showing that imposition of a modified sentence was made only in cases where the death penalty has been commuted.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the power to impose a modified punishment of providing any specific term of incarceration or till the end of the convict’s life as an alternative to death penalty can be exercised only by the High Court and the Supreme Court and not by any other inferior Court.
precedent_relied_upon: Union of India v. V. Sriharan alias Murugan & Ors. [2016 (7) SCC 1], Swamy Shraddananda (2) alias Murali Manohar Mishra v. State of Karnataka [2008 (13) SCC 767], Sahib Hussain alias Sahib Jan v. State of Rajasthan [2013 (9) SCC 778], Gurvail Singh alias Gala v. State of Punjab [2013 (10) SCC 631]
sentencing_rationale: The Court imposed a fixed-term sentence for a period of thirty years to ensure that the benefit of statutory remission is not available to the accused, considering the gravity and nature of the offence and all other relevant factors.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The Trial Court considered the appellant's age, family circumstances, and that this was his first offence as mitigating factors.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The Court noted the brutal nature of the offence, the shock to the conscience of the Court, and the need to uphold public confidence in the legal system.
other_sentence_order: The Court directed that the appellant shall undergo imprisonment for life and be released only after completing thirty years of actual sentence.
